content: Studies indicate that ACE inhibitors and ARBs are frequently not prescribed at their maximum tolerated doses, which can diminish their potential effectiveness in slowing the progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD). While ACE inhibitors and ARBs have been demonstrated to reduce mortality and slow CKD progression in diabetic patients with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) below 30 mL/min/1.73 m², their benefits are limited in patients who do not exhibit significant levels of albuminuria. To achieve the best therapeutic outcomes, it is crucial to titrate the dosage of these medications to the highest level that the patient can tolerate. If an increase in serum creatinine occurs without the presence of hyperkalemia, it is generally recommended to continue treatment unless the patient experiences significant adverse effects.
